description: Waffle chart of 100 squares in a 10-by-10 grid, each square one percent of North Carolina students in 2025: 35 teal squares for the 34.6 percent who reached Level 4 or 5 (college- and career-ready), the rest grey for Levels 1 to 3.

title.text: 35 of every 100 NC students reached Level 4 or 5
subtitle: Share of NC students at Level 4 or 5 (college- and
career-ready, CCR), 2025. Each square = 1% of students.

usermeta.source: Source: NCDPI accountability test scores (achievement levels, all subjects and grades, all students), 2025. Style-guide demo.

contrastExemptions.reason: Ruled by Andy 2026-07-30 during the contrast pass. This is a DELIBERATE deviation from Convention 5, which says to pair a #B7B9BB context fill with one of three mitigations; this chart uses none, for these reasons. #B7B9BB is 1.97:1 on white, but it is the REMAINDER mass, not a set of 65 items a reader must individually identify (contrast the dot map, where every dot is a school someone looks up). The color carrying the message -- teal #077890 at 5.12:1 -- passes, and the value is stated in the title ('35 of every 100'), which satisfies C5's own framing: the question is whether a reader can perceive the context marks exist, and against white gutters they can. C5 mitigation 2 (a #525A60 outline, used on the dot map and pictograph today) is UNAVAILABLE here: these cells abut, so the stroke slot must stay WHITE to serve Convention 9. C5 mitigation 1 (value labels on the context marks) WAS available and was considered and declined -- 100 cells cannot carry labels without becoming a table. Chose the convention over a redundant edge treatment rather than trading one house rule for another.
